scope: Proposition 2.5 (Saturated reduction) of the manuscript “The Deligne-Drinfeld conjecture” (preprints/The-Deligne-Drinfeld-conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 008 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5ae63f326803a634), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 8-9. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. statement: Let Kn = LieR⟨x, y⟩n, Ln = Wn ∩ Kn. Then Ln is a saturated finite free R-submodule of Kn, and its reduction embeds in Kn/2Kn. Writing its image as Ln, one has dimF2 Ln = dimQ Wn. (2.14) 8 More generally, for any rational subspace Vn ⊂ Wn, the lattice Mn = Vn ∩ Kn has an embedded reduction Mn ⊂ Ln of dimension dimQ Vn. Every element of Ln satisfies the reductions of the three defining identities. If n > 2, it also satisfies (2.4) and (2.5) after reduction, together with all formal coefficient consequences of these identities. In particular, putting z = x + y, [x, ψ(x, y) + ψ(z, y)] + [y, ψ(z, y)] = 0 (ψ ∈ Ln). (2.15)
